I submitted the verdict as verified: no spec text states what "valid" means for an entry that is programmed but not yet locked. I only read part of the RTL, so this rests on the specification search.

- **What the spec does say:** The hardware spec lists the trusted users (five configurable ones, the default user 0xFFFF_FFFF, and MCU). It also says untrusted users get an AXI error. The integration spec says the registers must be programmed and locked before SoC agents use the mailbox.
- **What it doesn't say:** It never says an unlocked entry is ignored by the filter. It also never says when a newly locked entry starts matching. Reading an unlocked entry as untrusted is an inference, not stated text.
- **RTL context:** In `src/mci/rtl/mci_reg_top.sv`, LOCK makes the entry read-only. The RTL also gates matching on LOCK (line 653), but I didn't read that in full.
- **Suggested fix:** Say explicitly that an unlocked entry is not used for matching and that a matching user gets an AXI error. Also say when a locked entry takes effect.

This was a close call; withdrawing was arguable, since the intended behavior can be inferred from the trusted-user text.
